samples.summary: Design doc still describes `resolvePageSetup` as a pass-through, after this change turned it into the validating/clamping read path
samples.evidence: `docs-pagination.md:96-97` reads: "A helper `resolvePageSetup(setup: PageSetup | undefined): PageSetup` returns `setup ?? DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP` (callers pass `doc.document.pageSetup`)." The diff makes it a substantive read-path contract: it substitutes defaults for non-finite/zero/negative dimensions and margins, and proportionally rescales margins that close the content box (`fitMargins`, new exported `MIN_CONTENT_PX`). The new "Page setup UI" section added by the diff documents only the *write*-side `RangeError` in `writePageSetup`, never the read-side clamp — so the canonical pagination doc now states the opposite of what the model does. Per CONTRIBUTING/design-doc discipline this behavioural change to the shared read path should be folded into the same doc that specifies it.
searchedFor: read docs/design/docs/docs-pagination.md added Page setup UI section

samples.summary: DOCX import geometry sanitisation/clamping is new document behaviour, outside the task's stated "pure wiring" scope and unrecorded in the DOCX design doc
samples.evidence: The originating task (`docs/tasks/active/20260829-docs-surface-existing-features-todo.md:3-5`) states "This task is pure wiring: no new document behaviour, no new file formats, no new model fields." The diff adds `sectPrLengthPx` and routes `parsePageSetup`'s result through `resolvePageSetup`, so an imported `.docx` whose `<w:pgMar>` exceeds the page now has its margins proportionally rescaled and non-numeric/negative/zero `<w:pgSz>` replaced by Letter defaults — a change to what an imported document looks like, not to how a shipped feature is surfaced. `docs/design/docs/docs-docx-import-export.md:315-321` still maps `<w:pgSz>`/`<w:pgMar>` straight to `PageSetup` with no mention of validation or clamping, and is not touched by this change.

samples.summary: Acceptance criterion "the keyboard shortcuts behave exactly as before" is not met: the format painter's capture semantics changed
samples.evidence: The task lists `- [x] The keyboard shortcuts behave exactly as before` (`20260829-docs-surface-existing-features-todo.md:57`), and its plan says the lift is a pure refactor ("The shortcuts must keep behaving exactly as they do now", line 33-34). The diff changes `captureFormatAtCursor` to take a `position` resolved by the new `formatSourcePosition()` (first *selected* character, table-rectangle-aware) instead of the caret, and additionally strips `image`, `pageNumber` and `href` from the buffer. `Mod+Shift+C` therefore picks up a different format than before for backward drags, block-end-anchored selections, cell rectangles, and any caret sitting on a link/image. Both changes look like improvements, but they are behaviour changes to the shortcut path the criterion pinned as unchanged, and only the structural-key strip is recorded in the task's review follow-ups.
searchedFor: read task acceptance criteria and review follow-ups

samples.summary: The "margins must leave room for content" rule is now stated in three places with three different thresholds instead of reusing the engine predicate the change introduces
samples.evidence: `assertUsablePageSetup` (editor.ts) exports/uses `MIN_CONTENT_PX` and rejects `left+right > width - MIN_CONTENT_PX`; the new dialog re-implements the rule as `parsed.left! + parsed.right! >= pageWidth` (docs-page-setup-dialog.tsx:152-156); the ruler keeps a separate 20 px floor. `MIN_CONTENT_PX` is exported from `@wafflebase/docs` precisely to keep the assert and the resolver in agreement, but the UI copy does not consume it — so a future change to the floor silently desynchronises the dialog's disabled-Apply state from what the write path will accept (a `RangeError` thrown out of a React submit handler). The engine-side check is correctly load-bearing; the duplication is in the UI copy of the same rule.
searchedFor: docs-pagination.md new Page setup UI section
